claims.statement: Directive (EU) 2019/944 requires Member States to allow and foster demand response through aggregation and recognizes incentive-based load changes.
PSE identifies facilitating demand-side-response services as an objective of Poland's capacity-market framework.

contrary_evidence: Existing aggregators may recruit assets directly, and residential-device value may be too small to fund installer bounties.

economics.acquisition_route: One-to-many distribution through heat-pump and EV installers, wholesalers, and installer quoting software.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 30000 activated devices producing 200 PLN retained annual revenue yields 6 million PLN recurring revenue by year six and can support founder equity above 5 million PLN without double-counting distributions.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 4 founder hours daily for product and aggregator operations, starting with the family installer as a bounded pilot.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 60-75% gross margin after installer bounty, device connectors, telemetry, settlement support, and consent operations.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: a 15000 PLN installer-network integration pays back after 100 activated assets.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis, including the capital figure: aggregators pay 250 PLN per activated device plus 1.5% of verified flexibility revenue.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Commissioning, annual re-enrollment, dispatch tests, and verified response events each generate revenue.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Device-specific dispatch and reliability histories improve enrollment selection and settlement confidence
fingerprint.customer: Flexibility aggregators seeking residential heat-pump and EV-charger capacity
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installer commissioning apps, wholesaler programs, and embedded quoting software
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Consent, enrollment, telemetry, and response-scoring exchange funded by activation bounty and revenue share
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The aggregator pays for a verified activation and later performance events
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An installer commissions a controllable device and obtains customer consent

founder_fit: The family installation company offers embedded-distribution access while data scoring and automation match the founder's strengths.
risks: Consent, cybersecurity, consumer contracts, device control, and settlement accuracy must be explicit before any activation.

structure.control_point: Customer consent and device identity captured at installer commissioning
structure.critical_dependency: Aggregator contracts, interoperable telemetry, and economics for small aggregated loads

thesis: Turn heat-pump and EV-charger commissioning into an aggregator enrollment event, with aggregators paying for activated assets and verified response while permissioned dispatch histories compound a device-level flexibility score.
title: FlexEnroll Installer Activation Exchange
uncertainties: No evidence yet establishes aggregator unit economics or reliable cross-brand device interoperability in Poland.
